items.title: Telangana climate conclave to be special feature of global summit
points: The forthcoming Invest Telangana Global Summit – 2026 will feature a special event, Telangana Climate Conclave.
To be held on December 8, the second day of the global summit, the conclave will witness participation of close to 200 scientists, experts from related fields and farmers.
Revanth Reddy wanted an exclusive discussion climate change and challenges posed by El Nino during the global summit.
The Chief Minister at a meeting with senior officials on Thursday reviewed the status of arrangements being made for the global summit and made several suggestions to the officials concerned.

Special invites should be sent to companies which evinced interest in investing in the State and officials concerned had been directed to ensure that a comprehensive plan for the successful conduct of the event was finalised by November 15.
Of the 575 firm that had been invited to attend the summit, 49 had evinced interest to attend the global summit.
Applications for the challenge would be accepted till November 20.

items.title: CM directs officials to begin Kaleshwaram barrage restoration works in December
points: Revanth Reddy with his Cabinet colleagues N.
Uttam Kumar Reddy and Ponnam Prabhakar, at a meeting in Hyderabad on Thursday.

Revanth Reddy has directed officials to take up restoration of the damaged Medigadda, Annaram and Sundilla barrages of the Kaleshwaram project strictly in accordance with the recommendations of national-level experts and the National Dam Safety Authority…
At a review meeting here, the Chief Minister asked officials to secure the final approvals by the end of November.

On the utilisation of Godavari waters through alternative arrangements, Mr. Reddy said the government had lifted water on an unprecedented scale through the Devadula and Sitarama lift irrigation schemes to prevent the downstream Godavari water from going…
While the previous government lifted an average of 9.57 tmc ft annually through Devadula, the average had increased to 18.13 tmc ft during the last three years, registering an increase of 89%.

items.title: Devotees banned from climbing Arunachala Hills in Tiruvannamalai on Maha Deepam day
points: District Collector Vandhana Garg told reporters on Thursday that the ban on climbing the hills on Maha Deepam was decided following forecast for heavy rain.
“The decision to prohibit devotees from climbing the hills has been taken to ensure the safety of people’s lives.
Around 50 lakh devotees are expected to visit the temple town during Karthigai Deepam festival,” Ms. Garg said.
In 2024, the ban came into force after seven persons, including children, died in a landslip that was triggered by cyclone Fengal in the hills.

Premalatha, Head, Centre for Soil Mechanics and Foundation Engineering, Anna University (Chennai), climbed the 2,668-foot-high hillock with police, forest and revenue officials to assess the condition of the hills.

“Relocation of people living in the hills to temporary shelters in the town will be done in the coming weeks, especially after Maha Deepam as heavy rains are expected later this month [November],” said a revenue official.

items.title: Revenue Minister orders assessment of cyclone damage on war-footing
points: Revenue Minister Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy has directed officials to assess the damage caused to crops, roads, irrigation facilities and electricity infrastructure by the heavy rains triggered by Cyclone Murasu in the erstwhile undivided Khammam district on…
The Minister asked the Collectors to submit detailed estimates of the cyclone-related damage to the government within the next two to three days.
He was addressing a review meeting with officials of Khammam and Bhadradri Kothagudem districts at Sathupalli in Khammam district on Thursday.
Earlier, he visited rain-affected areas in Sathupalli and Aswaraopet mandals along with local MLAs and officials.

Mr. Reddy appreciated the coordinated efforts of the district administration and other departments in preventing loss of life during the heavy rains over the past two days in Khammam and Bhadradri Kothagudem districts.

He noted that the State government strengthened the SDRF by training around 1,900 personnel drawn from the police and fire services departments and providing latest rescue equipment at a cost of around ₹260 crore - ₹270 crore.

items.title: World Trade Center township on the anvil for Chengalpattu
points: GTB Developers (GT Bharathi Urban Developers Pvt Ltd) announced that it has been granted a licence by the World Trade Centers Association (WTCA) to develop World Trade Center Chengalpattu.
This particular project is planned as an IT integrated township of 100 to 150 acre, rather than an industrial estate.
The project has an estimated value of ₹7,000 crore and will be developed in phases over approximately ten years.
The proposed masterplan includes commercial and IT office space, hospitality, residences and an education zone.
GTB is at an advanced stage of identifying and securing land for the project.
GTB is also pursuing a second World Trade Center development in Kanchipuram district, proposed across approximately 500 acres.
Unlike Chengalpattu, it is envisaged as an industrial World Trade Center, with manufacturing and data centre zones alongside infrastructure, education and hospitality.
GTB intends to explore the project under a public-private partnership (PPP) model, one of the structures under which World Trade Centers are developed globally.

items.title: Dhotis, sarees procured from cooperative societies in T.N. for Pongal, says Textiles Minister
points: Vijay Balaji at a press meet in Vellore on Thursday, November 5, 2026. | Photo Credit: VENKATACHALAPATHY C Minister of Handlooms and Textiles M.
Vijay Balaji on Thursday said that Tamil Nadu government will procure dhotis and sarees that will be distributed for PDS cardholders for Pongal only from Cooperative Societies in the State.
Addressing reporters here, Mr. Balaji denied claims that the State government plans to procure dhotis and sarees from other States to distribute them for beneficiaries.
In fact, the TVK led government has doubled the orders of dhotis and sarees produced by Cooperative Societies for the Pongal festival.
“Around 1.87 crore of dhotis and sarees will be procured from Cooperative Societies for distribution for PDS cardholders.
In other words, around 60,000 weavers will be benefitted as they would make these dhotis and sarees for the societies under the scheme,” he said.
The Minister also distributed government welfare assistance to a tune of Rs 63.30 crore to 585 women’s self-help groups in the district.

items.title: Hyderabad startup opens India’s first private space debris recovery facility
points: Hyderabad-based startup Cosmoserve Space on Thursday unveiled ‘Base 1’, touted as India’s first private facility and only the sixth in the world equipped with space-vision systems and microgravity simulation capabilities for satellite servicing and space…
The facility was inaugurated by Union Minister of State for Science & Technology and Space Dr. Jitendra Singh and Telangana IT and Industries Minister D.

Spread across multiple specialised laboratories, Base 1 combines satellite integration, space robotics, mission simulation and orbital capture technologies under one roof, enabling the company to design, build, test and operate satellite-servicing missions.
It houses an Orbital Rendezvous and Capture Lab, a Space Robotics Innovation Lab, an ISO Class 8 clean room for satellite integration, and a Mission Simulation and Control Centre.
Congratulating the company, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the facility reflects the growing technological capabilities of India’s private space startups.

Mr. Sridhar Babu said Hyderabad had emerged as a major spacetech hub, with more than 30 companies working on launch vehicles, space data centres, debris-removal systems and other advanced technologies.

items.title: Visa must for undocumented six non-Muslim communities who entered India before December 31, 2024: Home Ministry
points: The amended provision applies to persons belonging to the six minority communities who were compelled to seek shelter in India due to religious persecution or fear of religious persecution and entered the country on or before December 31, 2024.
“Provided that every such person shall be required to obtain an appropriate category of visa after their entry into India for their continued stay in India,” the notification said.

The 2025 exemption order had been issued under the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025, consolidating several earlier notifications that exempted members of these minority communities from prosecution under passport and foreigners laws.

The latest amendment aligns the exempted categories with the Citizenship (Amendment) Act (CAA), 2019, which fast-tracked Indian citizenship for the six non-Muslim minorities from the three neighbouring countries who entered India before December 31, 2014.

The amendment also revises provisions governing travel by Indian, Nepali and Bhutanese citizens, introduces a definition of the “Visa Manual”, and reorganises several categories of exemptions covering Tibetan refugees, registered Sri Lankan Tamil refugees…

items.title: Farmer, son electrocuted on illegal electrical fence in Vellore
points: A farmer and his son were electrocuted after they stepped on a snapped live wire of an illegal electric fence erected to prevent wild boars from entering the farmland in Palankuppam near Pernambut town in Vellore on Thursday.
Both, residents of the village, cultivated paddy and groundnuts on a five-acre plot they owned.
Initial inquiry revealed that Ranganathan, along with his son, went to the farmland to check the saplings in a new garden they had created recently.
The region has been witnessing heavy rains for the past few days following the onset of northeast monsoon.
As they were checking the saplings at various spots on the farmland, Ranganathan accidentally stepped on a snapped live wire on the ground and got electrocuted.
On hearing his cries, Suresh rushed to rescue his father but got electrocuted after stepping on the same wire.

items.title: APPCB steps up State-wide measures to curb air, noise pollution
points: The Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board (APPCB) has stepped up measures to curb air and noise pollution across the State, directing district administrations and police, transport and municipal authorities to enforce environmental regulations and monitor…

In a recent communication to Collectors, Magistrates, Superintendents of Police, Municipal Commissioners and Police Commissioners of Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam, the Board called for joint inspection teams to prevent the sale, transportation and use of…
It also directed officials to monitor air quality and noise levels in all district headquarters and towns, following orders issued on October 16.
The APPCB on Wednesday said its monitoring during Deepavali 2025 had recorded PM10 levels of up to 238 micrograms per cubic metre and PM2.5 levels of 138 micrograms per cubic metre in Visakhapatnam.

Only green crackers approved by the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research-National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (CSIR-NEERI) will be permitted in cities and towns where air quality is moderate or better, subject to court directions.

items.title: ZPTC, MPTC polls peaceful in ASR, Visakhapatnam; turnout 82.51% in Visakhapatnam, provisional 59.98% in ASR
points: In ASR district, voting began at 7 a.m. for 11 ZPTC and 172 MPTC seats and was conducted in a free and peaceful manner, officials said, with no untoward incident.
Turnout rose from 12.3% at 9 a.m. to 27.6% at 11 a.m., 45.4% at 1 p.m. and 57.2% at 3 p.m.
By 5 p.m., 59.98% of the electors in the 11 mandals had voted, according to provisional figures.
In Visakhapatnam, 1,34,000 of the 1,62,407 electors, or 82.51%, exercised their franchise in the elections to four ZPTC and 53 MPTC seats, according to final figures from the district administration.
The turnout was up from 71.23% at 3 p.m.
Anandapuram recorded the highest turnout at 84.76%, followed by Padmanabham (81.89), Pendurthi (81.40) and Bheemunipatnam (80.97).
A total of 203 polling stations were set up, with 13 candidates in the fray for the ZPTC seats and 117 for the MPTC seats.

points: FILE PHOTO | Photo Credit: FILE PHOTO Visakhapatnam MP M.

Sribharat on Thursday urged the newly elected corporators from the NDA parties of the Visakhapatnam North Assembly constituency to make public service their foremost priority and work sincerely for the development of their wards.

“Corporators should remain accessible to citizens, monitor local issues and work with the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) officials to resolve problems relating to drinking water, sanitation, roads and drainage”, he said.

Mr. Sribharat said the alliance’s victory was the result of coordination and unity—from seat-sharing to the selection of candidates— between the Telugu Desam Party (TDP), the Jana Sena Party (JSP) and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
Vishnu Kumar Raju for ensuring a fair and balanced approach while choosing candidates with their strengths in view.

items.title: Young India Police School to begin full-fledged classes in new block next academic year
points: Director General of Police CV Anand, along with ADG (Law and Order) Mahesh Bhagwat, ADG (OCTOPUS) Anil Kumar and IGP L.
Gajarao Bhupal at the Young India Police School (YIPS) in Manchirevula construction site. | Photo Credit: By Arrangement Director General of Police C.V.

items.title: Young dancers enthrall audience at Kaladarshini cultural festival in Vijayawada
points: The 23rd Kaladarshini Cultural Festival witnessed an impressive display of youthful talent during the Western Group Dance competitions, which attracted enthusiastic participation from students representing various educational institutions, on Thursday…

The Andhra Loyola Engineering College auditorium turned into a vibrant stage as young dancers delivered energetic and captivating performances, showcasing their creativity, coordination and artistic skills.
The participants impressed the audience with well-choreographed routines, synchronised movements, and innovative dance styles, earning loud applause from parents, teachers, and fellow students.
The competition offered a valuable platform for students to showcase their talents, enhance their confidence, foster teamwork and appreciate cultural diversity.

Parents, teachers, and participants appreciated the efforts of Kaladarshini Fine Arts Institute in organising the festival and providing opportunities for young people to explore their creative abilities and celebrate cultural expression.

items.title: Environmental organisation flags dilution of safeguards in rules regarding conversion of agricultural land in T.N.
points: Environmental organisation Poovulagin Nanbargal has raised concerns over the latest amendments to the rules governing the conversion of agricultural land for non-agricultural purposes in Tamil Nadu.
It said that the changes could weaken the scrutiny involved in approving such conversions.
The organisation said in a statement that the government had been taking steps to simplify the procedures for converting agricultural land.
It questioned the removal of the earlier requirement for the District Collector to personally inspect the land and examine various factors before granting approval.

The concerns follow the State government’s latest amendments to the Tamil Nadu Change of Land Use (From Agriculture to Non-agriculture Purposes in Non-planning Areas) Rules, 2017, issued through a G.O. by the Housing and Urban Development Department on…
Under the amended rules, applications for developing wetlands for non-agricultural purposes must be submitted through the Single Window Portal, along with several documents.

items.title: Centre tells Supreme Court it may set up a panel to review UGC equity on campus regulations
points: The UGC notified the 2026 Regulations in January after consultations, superseding the 2012 framework.

File. | Photo Credit: Sushil Kumar Verma The Union government is “contemplating” having a special committee review the University Grants Commission (Promotion of Equity in Higher Education Institutions) Regulations, 2026, it said in a submission to the…

In a brief hearing before a Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, for the government, sought more time to come back with a comprehensive response, but added that the Centre was examining criticism about the 2026…
In January 2026, the top court had stayed the Regulations, finding them “too sweeping” and vague.
It had ordered that the University Grants Commission (Promotion of Equity in Higher Education Institutions) Regulations, 2012, would continue to be in force.
The Court had further issued notice to the government and the University Grants Commission (UGC) on separate petitions challenging Regulation 3(c) of the 2026 Regulations.

items.title: Cabinet approves 30-year lease of four acres in High Grounds to Bangalore Turf Club
points: The four-acre area currently houses the club facilities and includes a heritage structure.
While agreeing to shift racing activities to the Kunigal Stud Farm, the BTC had sought six acres to continue its club activities and off-course betting centre.
However, the government agreed to provide four acres.
Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Minister Eshwar Khandre told presspersons after the Cabinet meeting that the government had approved the lease proposal.
“The club has also sought some time to relocate the racing activities to Kunigal,” he said.
The development follows an earlier decision of the State government not to extend the lease term to the BTC, and offered land to build a racecourse at the Kunigal Stud Farm.
After initial reluctance, the BTC agreed to shift the club operations to Kunigal but sought six acres to continue with club activities and off course betting centre on the current premises.

items.title: Four killed, two missing as SUV plunges into river near Gangotri
points: The passengers, reportedly from Gujarat, were travelling to the Gangotri temple.
According to police, the accident took place on the Gangotri National Highway when the vehicle reportedly went out of control and plunged into the river.
Rescue teams recovered four bodies from the riverbank during an operation involving the local police, State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) and emergency medical services.
The deceased have been identified as Ashokben Patel (49), Rutika Ashokbhai Patel (19), Ghanshyambhai Sarwaliya (32), from Gujarat and the driver, Surendra Singh, a resident of Haridwar.
The two missing passengers are Sudaben Ashokbhai Patel (45) and Kiranben Vishalbhai Patel (34).
Another passenger, 17-year-old Vedant Ashokbhai Patel, was rescued in an unconscious state.
He was initially taken to the Primary Health Centre in Bhatwari and later referred to a higher medical facility for further treatment.
District Magistrate Prashant Arya said medical teams had been placed on alert as the search for the missing passengers continued.

items.title: CJP leaders Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka appear before Delhi Police in Jantar Mantar trespassing cases
points: After appearing before the investigators, Mr. Ranka said the two leaders will cooperate with the probe.
“Today’s questioning was part of a routine investigation into the events of October 13.
The two leaders had earlier been arrested and sent to judicial custody after entering the denotified Jantar Mantar protest site and waving the national flag with 12 other persons on October 13.
The police had also said that their actions violated a peace bond they had signed on October 11.
Two FIRs were registered at the Connaught Place and Parliament Street police stations on October 13.
The cases were subsequently transferred to the Crime Branch, which had summoned the two leaders for questioning on October 22.
The two leaders were released from Tihar jail on October 21 after furnishing personal bonds and surety bonds of ₹50,000 each.
Special Executive Magistrate Ritu Raj ordered their release on the condition that the bonds would remain in force until the conclusion of the inquiry into the Jantar Mantar trespassing case.

items.title: INS Sahyadri reaches Japan for multilateral naval exercise MALABAR 2026
points: According to the Indian Navy, the warship, part of the Eastern Fleet, was accorded a warm welcome by the Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force (JMSDF).
The ceremony was attended by Vice Admiral Yagi Koji, Commandant of Yokosuka District, and R.
Madhu Sudan, Deputy Chief of the Indian Mission in Japan.

The exercise will provide an opportunity to the participating navies to enhance operational coordination, strengthen interoperability, and exchange professional expertise through a series of engagements during the harbour and sea phases.

The harbour phase will involve professional interactions and coordinated planning, while the subsequent sea phase will see INS Sahyadri operate alongside participating naval units from the U.S. , Australia and Japan.

A press release by theMinistry of Defence said that the engagements are aimed at strengthening mutual trust and maritime cooperation among the four countries and contributing to a secure and stable Indo-Pacific region.

items.title: Green gram procurement centre opens in Santhemarahalli in Chamarajanagar
points: Produce conforming to Fair Average Quality (FAQ) standards — concerning moisture content, foreign matter and damaged grains — will be purchased at this centre at the rate of ₹8,780 per quintal.
The Karnataka State Co-operative Marketing Federation, Bengaluru, will procure the produce.
The amount will be credited to the bank account linked to the farmer’s Aadhaar card.
Farmers must submit copies of their Record of Rights, Tenancy and Crops (RTC), Aadhaar card, bank passbook and a passport-size photograph, along with their FRUIT ID, at the time of registration.
Only farmers whose names are recorded as green gram cultivators in the RTC are eligible to avail this facility.
Procurement will continue for 90 days, while registration will remain open for 80 days.
A maximum of four quintals per acre, subject to an overall ceiling of 20 quintals per farmer, will be procured under the MSP.
For further details, contact 9449864455, according to information provided by the Chamarajanagara APMC.

points: Polling for the MPTC/ZPTC elections continued until 8 p.m. in many parts of Kakinada district on Thursday, as farmers and agriculture labourers turned up at polling station after they returned from their fields, which were affected by the cyclones Arnab…
Although polling was scheduled to end at 5 p.m.

items.title: Foreign Secretary Misri sets stage for Nepal PM’s upcoming India visit
points: Indian Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri with Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah at Singhadurbar, Nepal, on November 5, 2026.

Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri on Thursday (November 5, 2026) met Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah in Kathmandu, with discussions focused on “possible outcomes and initiatives” from the upcoming visit of the Himalayan nation’s leader to New Delhi.
Concluding his official engagements in Nepal that spanned Wednesday and Thursday, Mr. Misri also met Nepal Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle and Foreign Minister Sisir Khanal.
Mr. Misri held detailed talks with his host, Nepali Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai, on the “mutually beneficial partnership” between India and Nepal.

Mr. Shah had earlier this year highlighted the border dispute with India in the Lipulekh-Kalapai-Limpiyadhura area that is part of India’s Uttarakhand but claimed by Nepal as a sticking point in ties.
The Nepali leaders expressed “gratitude for India’s swift and substantial humanitarian and technical assistance in the aftermath of the Bhotekoshi floods”, the joint press release stated.

items.title: Agniveer scheme not rolled back, all eligible recruits to be absorbed after six years: MoD
points: At the end of the second engagement period, all those willing and meeting the prescribed eligibility criteria will be absorbed as regular soldiers, officials said.

According to Ministry of Defence sources, the scheme remains unchanged in its basic structure, with an additional engagement period of two years introduced for the 75% of Agniveers who are not absorbed into the regular cadre after their initial four-year…
At the end of the second engagement period, all those willing and meeting the prescribed eligibility criteria will be absorbed as regular soldiers, officials said.
Addressing concerns over the seniority of the 75% Agniveers who will serve for six years before joining the regular cadre, a Defence Ministry official said their seniority would be protected.
The official also confirmed that there would be no numerical cap on the absorption of the remaining 75% after the second engagement period.

items.title: Two more bodies recovered from trekking route in Uttarakhand
points: According to the district administration, the two bodies recovered on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) were identified as Rintu Mondol, 40, and Uday Ghosh, 30, both residents of Bankura, West Bengal.
Six bodies, including the two from today, have been recovered for the site so far.
Eight people from an expedition of 13 went missing after heavy snowfall and multiple avalanches cut off the route.

Among the people who went missing were seven trekkers —Tapas Bauri, Ratan Ghosh, Mr. Mondal, Mr. Ghosh, Manoj Khawas, all from West Bengal; Vartika and Deepika Verma, sisters from lucknow — and local guide Siddharth Rana.

Four support staff were rescued on October 31 near Kachchi Dhang.

items.title: Devi Shetty conferred with France’s National Order of Merit
points: The honour was presented by Marc Lamy, Consul General of France in Bengaluru, at a ceremony held at Narayana Health City on Wednesday.

Dr. Shetty was recognised for extending vaccination and logistical support to the French Consulate and the wider French community during the pandemic, demonstrating solidarity at a time of unprecedented challenges.
“We are delighted to recognise Dr. Devi Shetty for his generosity and unwavering support to the French community in Bengaluru during the pandemic.
His actions reflect the true spirit of solidarity and the enduring friendship between France and India,” Mr. Lamy said.
Accepting the honour, Dr. Shetty said he was grateful to the French government and acknowledged the contribution of Narayana Health’s teams in extending assistance during the pandemic.

items.title: SEBI allows net settlement of funds for MFs from April
points: AMCs can offset eligible purchase and sale obligations within settlement cycles from April 2027. | Photo Credit: DHIRAJ SINGH SEBI has allowed mutual fund schemes to adopt net settlement of funds for outright transactions in the cash market from April 2027.
The move will reduce temporary funding requirements, improve liquidity management, and enhance operational efficiency for asset management companies, according to the circular issued on Thursday.
Under the new framework, MF schemes will be allowed to net their purchase and sale fund obligations arising from eligible transactions in the same settlement cycle.
